emerging_technology: Agentic AI: language-model systems choosing tool actions and using observations across a bounded multi-step task.
intended_application: Proposed chart-review assistant: compare business charts with approved source tables, use read-only SQL/spreadsheet tools, and draft correction notes. Human approval is required; no autonomous publication.
business_need: Investigate whether chart-review effort can be reduced while retaining traceability and analyst accountability.
management_question: What significance classification is defensible for this defined system, with what confidence, and how much should it influence this organization's present chart-review decision?
time_horizon: Four-week feasibility investigation; twelve-month organizational review; separate long-range societal question without a realization date.
additional_context: Constructed teaching case continuing the TW4 common chart-review application. No local pilot, measured savings, agent accuracy or institutional collapse is supplied. Use this bounded source packet, checked 2026-10-20; sources describe mechanisms and limits, not chart-review outcomes. S0: System, barrier and suppression gates; formal six-criterion assessment after dissolution; two distinct human-life tiers; prospective and retrospective modes. Limit: Instructor working framework, not academic consensus or empirical proof about this agent. The generative-AI calibration is not inherited. The full chapter is not redistributed. Source: Local instructor chapter | S1: Demonstrates interleaved reasoning/action on bounded tasks with stated baselines. Limit: Not current chart-review performance, global novelty, tenfold full-workflow benefit or civilizational dependence. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629v3 | S2: Distinguishes model-directed tool processes from predefined workflows and identifies complexity tradeoffs. Limit: Vendor guidance, not independent validation. The page warns that tooling has changed. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents | S3: Documents a historical gap on tool-using assistant questions. Limit: The tested older setup is not an October 2026 frontier estimate, chart QA or universal failure rate. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983v1 | S4: Horizon measures difficulty indexed by human task time at a specified success probability. Limit: Not AI runtime, a speed ratio or general job coverage. Predominantly software/ML/cyber tasks; page no longer actively updated. Source: https://metr.org/time-horizons/ | S5: Later developer productivity estimates have selection and measurement limitations. Limit: Historical slowdown does not establish current universal failure; later uncertainty does not prove a tenfold gain. Source: https://metr.org/blog/2026-02-24-uplift-update/ | S6: Final article reports 15% mean productivity gain among 5,172 human support workers. Limit: Single-firm human assistance, not autonomous software agents, chart-review evidence or tenfold gain. Do not combine earlier working-paper counts with this final version. Source: https://academic.oup.com/qje/article/140/2/889/7990658
users_stakeholders: Business analysts, managers, security staff and named report owners
capabilities_constraints: Approved BI tables and manual analyst checks exist. Sensitive data; no approved external model environment. Financial products and relationship services earn revenue; chart review is an internal support activity, not a sold service. Before environment authorization use only public or synthetic material; no sensitive-data trial is authorized.
risk_consequence_context: Misleading reports may harm decisions; unauthorized data disclosure is consequential. Synthetic draft examples are reversible. Human report ownership stays in place.
